title: Mahatma Gandhi and Kasturba at Aga Khan Palace: Sacrifice and Silent Courage
summary: In February 1944, inside the Aga Khan Palace internment camp, Kasturba Gandhi took her final breath in Gandhi's arms, marking an unshakeable testament to lifelong shared sacrifice.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 139: காந்தியும் கஸ்தூர்பாவின் இறுதிச் சடங்கும்: “இப்போது போனால் பா மன்னிக்கமாட்டார்”
full_text:
On the evening of February 22, 1944, inside the historic Aga Khan Palace in Pune—converted by the colonial authorities into a prison camp following the Quit India declaration—a profound silence fell over the courtyards.

Kasturba Gandhi, frail and exhausted after months of severe illness, lay dying. For more than six decades, she had been Mohandas Gandhi’s companion, confidante, and the unsung pillar of the satyagraha movement, enduring South African jails, ashram austerity, and countless national campaigns.

Her head rested gently in Gandhi's lap. Devoted companions wept quietly, but Gandhi remained serene, stroking her forehead with tender devotion. As her breathing slowed, Kasturba looked into his eyes and whispered her final blessings:
"Bapu, do not grieve. Finish the work of India's freedom."

Moments later, she breathed her last. The British jail superintendent approached Gandhi with polite deference:
"Mr. Gandhi, the government is prepared to permit the body to be taken outside for a public funeral."

Gandhi looked up, his voice steady with solemn dignity:
"No. Ba lived as a prisoner of conscience and died as a soldier of freedom in this internment camp. She will be cremated here within these prison walls, by our own hands. There is no sacred ground more fitting for a freedom fighter than the earth where she gave her last breath."

In the face of devastating personal loss, Gandhi demonstrated the profound fortitude that anchored India's struggle for emancipation.
